source_note: Suspicious RubyGems from the operator hunt repo (silent-locus). May campaign: gem nodes subtype diffend-harvest in data/lanes/rubygems-goimport-campaign/events.jsonl (615 versions, triple-checked disk count), wave by earliest first_seen date (2026-05-11 rehearsal, 2026-05-12 burst); pin files add versions only (first_seen null for pin-only versions). node.status dead is mapped to yanked=true; the pins-diffend header states these were yanked from rubygems.org. go_import_target/VCS come from raw/gem-ioc-hits.jsonl fingerprints (go-import-repo, go-import-vcs, council-domain); gems with no IOC row carry payload_type null, not a guess. Builder detail for the three verified runner gems follows the Sept triple-check note. June-18 rows come from raw/gem-june18-wayback.jsonl pre-removal metadata (gems yanked, bytes unrecoverable); the 17th June name (16 Nightingale + 1 new) was not recovered from the files checked and is NOT included. July-7 JFrog specimens are report text, NOT locally captured bytes (their campaign gem bytes were found nowhere in our holdings); July-7-window Diffend gems are third-party test/researcher gems, explicitly NOT GemStuffer campaign gems. Probe-family rows carry their rescan triage verdicts. EXCLUDED: live legit contrast gems (json, oai, thor and the aws-sdk/gitlab/google-apis families, which appear only as contrast), the full 3,025-row JFrog GemStuffer CSV (third-party list; used only for jfrog_xray_id enrichment on overlapping names), and an unparsed ElasticSearch-style dump under docs/notes that may hold additional names but was not used as a curated source. No credential, key, token, or secret value is included anywhere in this file; author strings are registry metadata as recorded in lane files. V2 ADDENDUM (2026-10-27): full sweep. The ElasticSearch-style dump (docs/notes/hidden_files/lane1/jfrog.json, 3,025 hits) holds exactly the same name set as the JFrog CSV — zero names beyond the CSV, so the two are one source viewed twice. The JFrog CSV is now an inclusion source, not enrichment-only, with per-row source_grade: observed (our lane/note record, no CSV match), overlap (our record + JFrog CSV), third-party-list (JFrog CSV entry with no lane corroboration). CSV-only rows carry wave null and payload null: the CSV has no per-name dates, and JFrog's per-day counts span May 5–July 7, so wave attribution per row would be a guess; the 1,569 CSV-only names our libraries.io probe found:true are graded overlap with the probe file cited in provenance, the other 851 stay third-party-list. June-18 grows 16 -> 83 from the gem83 reconciliation CSV (all 83 in JFrog, Xray IDs agree with v1 on the 16 overlap rows); the v1 "17th June name" framing is superseded by that reconciled 83-name set. GHSA adds zero rows: gemstuffer-shaped GHSA names outside v1 are all in the CSV except "sarif", which is excluded (name collides with a well-known legit gem; GHSA-heuristic only, no lane corroboration). qa-authz/qa-scope probes remain patterns only (no exact names in notes or lane files) and stay excluded. Lane re-sweep (events.jsonl, graph-nodes, pins, ioc-hits) adds zero names beyond v1 except the legit contrast trio (json, oai, thor), which stay excluded. March-7 modality adds 4 specimens; rgscan upload/yank integrity tests add 2. No credential, key, token, or secret value is included anywhere in this file; author strings are registry metadata as recorded in lane files.
